title: The Mechanics of Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification refers to a society's categorization of its people into rankings based on factors such as wealth, income, and power. This hierarchical structure is rarely random; instead, it involves systemic arrangements that allocate resources and opportunities unequally among groups.

The primary dimensions used to analyze this system include class, status, and power. While economic class often relates to material possessions and job type, social status pertains more to perceived honor or prestige within a community. Power represents the ability to influence others and enforce one's will on them.

Different societies utilize various systems of stratification, ranging from closed caste systems, which restrict movement between groups entirely, to open class systems, which theoretically allow for individual upward mobility based on merit or economic achievement.
